subject: pol-dy
title: POL.DY.-----CULT.INFO.F.
description: Diagram in MP(I)-37 — the section identifying the spectacle-diversion cycle's information-regulation mechanisms. The prose immediately above the diagram names what the crossing makes structural: 'The utilization of source transfer — gradualism — words (or their use in outlets like western criticism) — misdocumentation — and outright lies are only a few of what I call the available procedures that have been established in the west as factors to regulate culture. It is for this reason that alternative creativity must first come through the spectacle-diversion cycle of information regulation before the public can actually be exposed to its particulars.' The crossing diagrams that spectacle-diversion structurally: POL-DY (political dynamics — the working political-mechanism that regulates information) is crossed with CULT-INFO-F (culture information focus). POL-DY sits on the left with the subject-arrow; its main line runs right to CULT-INFO-F, the partner-axis. (R)INFO-TRNS (the reality of information transference) rises from the main line, with DOC (documentation) branching from it and CULT-SOLD (culture solidification) from DOC's line. POL-P (political policies) drops from the main line, with CULT-O (culture order) branching from POL-P's line and EXTN-D (existential definition) from CULT-O's line. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) drops from the main line at lower-left; AF-COMP (affinity compression) branches from AF-DY's line, (R)P-FC (the reality of particular focus) from AF-COMP's line, and DYM-SEP (dynamic separation) from P-FC's line. Structural argument: the upper diagonal INFO-TRNS → DOC → CULT-SOLD is the *misdocumentation chain* — political-dynamics routes information-transference through documentation into culture-solidification. This is the structural shape of 'source transfer — gradualism — words.' The 'sophistication of the western political position' the prose names is exactly this: every upper-chain edge and every lower-chain edge is structurally held by available procedures.
